original_question: In the notation of 21.52, let Autt(Γ) be the set of permutations τT∈ SD such that(a, b) ∼ (aτ, bτ) whenever |ab| = t for a, b ∈ D. Clearly, Aut(Γ) = t Autt(Γ). Is it true that for every finite simple group G we have Aut(Γ) = Aut2(Γ) ∩ Autp(Γ), where {2, p} are the two minimal prime divisors of |G|?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.53 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)", with notation inherited from Problem 21.52.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official wording. It correctly identifies the auxiliary sets Aut_t(Γ), the relation Aut(Γ) = intersection over t of Aut_t(Γ), and the specific question asking whether one only needs the cases t = 2 and t = p, where {2, p} are the two smallest prime divisors of the group order.
missing_details: The draft is not stand-alone because it omits the setup from Problem 21.52: L must be a finite non-abelian simple group.
It omits that D is a conjugacy class of involutions in L.
It omits that Γ is the complete graph with vertex set D.
It omits the edge-coloring/equivalence relation on edges: (a, b) ~ (c, d) if and only if |ab| = |cd|.
It omits the definition of Aut(Γ) as the group of color-preserving permutations of D, i.e. permutations τ in Sym(D) such that (a, b) ~ (aτ, bτ) for every edge (a, b).
It should specify that Sym(D) is the full permutation group on D.
It should specify what values of t are being intersected over: namely, those integers that occur as |ab| for some pair of distinct involutions a, b in D.
The OCR-corrupted identity in the draft should be restored to Aut(Γ) = intersection over t of Aut_t(Γ).

To stay faithful to the paper’s notation, the group symbol should be used consistently: 21.52 uses L, while 21.53 switches to G; a refined stand-alone version should pick one symbol and keep it fixed.
Because the notation comes from 21.52, the intended scope is the involution-class construction for finite simple groups admitting such a class; without that context, the question is underspecified.
refined_question: Let L be a finite non-abelian simple group, let D be a conjugacy class of involutions in L, and let Γ be the complete graph with vertex set D. Define an equivalence relation on the edge set of Γ by declaring (a, b) ~ (c, d) if and only if |ab| = |cd|. Let Aut(Γ) be the group of all permutations τ in Sym(D) such that (a, b) ~ (aτ, bτ) for every edge (a, b). For each integer t that occurs as |ab| for some a, b in D, define Aut_t(Γ) to be the set of all permutations τ in Sym(D) such that (a, b) ~ (aτ, bτ) whenever |ab| = t. Then Aut(Γ) is the intersection over all such t of Aut_t(Γ). If p is the second-smallest prime divisor of |L|, is it always true that Aut(Γ) = Aut_2(Γ) ∩ Aut_p(Γ)?
justification: The draft is aiming exactly at Problem 21.53, not at the broader neighboring Problem 21.52. Problem 21.53 asks the same intersection-reduction question that appears in your draft, while Problem 21.52 provides the hidden notation and definitions needed to make that question self-contained: the finite non-abelian simple group, the involution class D, the complete graph Γ, the edge-coloring by orders |ab|, and the definition of Aut(Γ). So the paper-faithful refinement is simply to restore the missing setup from 21.52 and present 21.53 verbatim in a self-contained way.
